title: Nano Flow Manifest
description: Shared contract between Storyboard AI (planner) and AutoFlow Reel extension (operator). Identical copy lives in both repos under docs/nano-flow-pipeline/. See DESIGN.md.

board_aspect_ratio.description: Storyboard board/sheet format. Always landscape and independent from final video aspect_ratio.

thumbnail_aspect_ratio.description: Thumbnail delivery format; independent from the video aspect ratio.

social_posts.description: Reuses the existing Storyboard SocialPosts shape verbatim (tiktok / youtube_shorts / facebook_reel).

character_style.description: Exact character and environment visual-medium lock selected in Storyboard; repeated inside image/video prompts for consumers that ignore project metadata.

assets.description: Reference images declared once per project. Each shot references entries by id. image=null means the slot is declared but the user attaches the real image on the extension side.

production_state.description: Additive canonical Production State. Legacy consumers may ignore it; prompt compilers use it as script-derived state authority.

export_qa.description: Non-blocking export QA snapshot. A valid manifest may be exported with warnings; consumers may ignore this additive field.

id.description: Stable id referenced by shots, e.g. char_lan

image.description: data: URI or null (user attaches later in extension)

wardrobe.description: Characters only — the story-locked outfit. The extension builds one full-body wardrobe sheet (identity photo + this outfit) and reuses it as the reference for every keyframe so face AND clothes stay identical. Empty ⇒ extension derives an outfit from the scene.

location_views.description: Legacy environments-only A2 pair. Kept for compatibility.

location_sheet_prompt.description: Preferred environments-only A2 contract: generate ONE 16:9 sheet containing exactly two clearly distinct, character-free angles of the same set.

locationView.description: A2 — one character-free establishing view of a location (see asset.location_views).

angle.description: "wide" (full establishing) | "alt" (second angle of the SAME place).

prompt.description: Prompt (100% Storyboard) to generate this EMPTY location image — no people, no product; same set, materials, furniture and lighting as its scenes.

refSelector.description: Which declared assets to attach at a given step.

use_generated_storyboard.description: Use the Nano-Banana-generated image from step A as the video FIRST FRAME.

environments.description: Default empty — background already baked into the keyframe (see DESIGN.md §6).

products.description: Default empty — enable only when exact logo/label fidelity is needed.

scene.description: Schema 4.1 — one SCENE inside a shot, generated as its own Nano Banana image.

camera.description: Camera framing for this scene, e.g. "[CLOSE]".

action.description: The scripted action/moment this scene depicts.

image_prompt.description: Prompt (100% Storyboard) to generate THIS scene's image — shot's locked context at this scene's moment.

image_refs.description: Assets to attach for this scene's image gen.

location_id.description: Environment asset id for this scene (a shot may span locations).

transition_from_prev.description: How this scene continues from the previous scene (or prior shot for scene 1).

storyboard_name.description: Name given to the Nano Banana image, ordered.

continuity_mode.description: Schema 4.0 — continuity decision for the boundary entering this shot.

location_id.description: Environment asset id this shot's scenes default to (per-location memory/background ref).

storyboard_prompt.description: STEP A — single-image FALLBACK keyframe prompt. When scenes[] is present the extension renders per-scene images instead; this is kept for consumers that ignore scenes.

scenes.description: Schema 4.1 — ordered SCENES of this shot, one generated image each (built from beats). Replaces the single-keyframe collapse; a shot may span locations.

end_storyboard_prompt.description: STEP A2 (optional) — prompt for the END keyframe of a transform shot. When present, the video uses start_end_frame mode: Veo interpolates start→end. Omit for a normal single-keyframe shot.

image_refs.description: STEP A — which assets feed the image generation (shared by start + end keyframes).

video_prompt.description: STEP B — full Veo prompt (written 100% by Storyboard). Either flat prose (string) or the structured Veo clip JSON (object); the extension stringifies objects into Flow's prompt box.

characters_in_scene.description: Exact character names on screen (mirrors Storyboard VideoSegment.characters_in_scene).

video_refs.description: STEP B — which refs to attach when generating the video.

voice.description: Maps to the extension voice list (auto/achernar/achird/...).

wardrobe_change.description: A visibly motivated change of clothes starting at this shot: { "CharacterName": "new outfit" }. The extension regenerates that character's full-body wardrobe sheet with the new outfit and uses it from this shot onward. Omit/null when unchanged.

state_authority.description: Canonical script/state contract embedded into both prompts. Authority flows script -> Production State -> video prompt -> storyboard board; never in reverse.
